column4: Volume, area, and L_high taken from Glicken (1996), 2.5 km3, 64 km2, 29km,  respectively. The landslide occurred retrogressively in three slide blocks. Rapid depressurization from the first block ("unroofing") led to initiation of lateral blast, which burst through the second block. Eyewitnesses couldn't see the third block, but it's thought to have failed in many discrete successive failures.

This event was complex, signals are from the rockslide-avalanche, but also pyroclastic flows, lahars, and the lateral blast and initial M5.1 earthquake that may have triggered the landslide (or may have been the landslide itself). Many of the short period stations were recorded as triggers so there are gaps in the data (EH?, SL?). Teleseismic data is available in complete records but at low sample rates (LH?).
Lower L estimate of 23km taken from Christiansen and Peterson (1981).
Best estimate of L (24 km), H (2.55 km) and total area (60 km2) from Siebert (1984). H/L of 0.11.

Mass and start time of debris avalanche (15:32:11 UTC) taken from Kanamori and Given (1982). They also show that the radiation pattern of the long period teleseismic waves generated by the debris avalanche were consistent with a single force mechanism, they state that these long period waves were likely generated by the initial stage of the debris avalanche, then long period waves were primarily generated by the lateral blast. Events following the blast they suggest are effects of the landslide during its deceleration stage and also explosions.
Upper estimate of mass from Brodsky and others (2003).
Crown and toe coordinates based on maps from Voight and others (1981)
Low estimate of mass from Ekstrom and Stark (2013)

Raw waveforms from closest stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

High frequency (1-5 Hz) ground velocity waveforms for station response from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Waveforms are corrected for station response after removing the mean. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Clipped waveforms have not been removed before station correction so check raw plots before interpreting high amplitude signals.
Spectrograms of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present

Multitaper spectra (same units as Power Spectral Density) of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Linear trend was removed and a taper was applied before generating spectra. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Since station response was not removed to avoid adding artifacts at low frequencies for short and intermediate period stations, the lower frequency amplitudes should be interpreted with care.

Teleseismic velocity waveforms from closest stations with detections. Waveforms are corrected for station response after detrending. Zero mean cosine filter (1/200., 1/100., 0.5, 0.25) in Hz applied with station correction may cause acausal arrivals.
